phases.title: Homelab web hosting (Proxmox + OPNsense + Cloudflare Tunnel)
phases.summary: Turning a Proxmox host behind OPNsense into a self-hosted replacement for a VPS/cloud web server - Tailscale-connected, an isolated LXC webserver, all public exposure through Cloudflare Tunnel with zero port-forwarding. Same "real, demonstrable infrastructure" thread as the rest of this project, not a toy.

steps.label: Discovered OPNsense ("fw1") was already tailnet-connected, advertising all 3 LAN subnet routes - box just never accepted them
Enabled route acceptance on box - full reachability to the Proxmox network via OPNsense's existing routing
Proxmox ("pveopti") joined the tailnet with its own dedicated identity, not just reachable via the routed subnet
SSH key-based auth to Proxmox established - root password never touched this session at any point
Diagnosed and fixed a physical switch trunking gap blocking VLAN20/30 (ruled out Proxmox/OPNsense config via container, VM, and cross-VLAN tests first)
Confirmed OPNsense's actual VLAN layout, placed new webserver on isolated VLAN20 - firewall rule verified to block mgmt/other VLANs while allowing internet egress
LXC container (web01): nginx + its own Tailscale identity + cloudflared - all live and verified
New Cloudflare Tunnel - alwaysgivealwaysget.com (dormant domain, reactivated for real use) served through it end-to-end over HTTPS
Internal DNS live on int.nunchimangchi.com (AdGuard Home rewrites) - resolves internally only, confirmed empty from public resolvers

Found the dormant ACME DNS-01 setup already existed (wildcard cert for *.int.nunchimangchi.com, live Cloudflare token) - verified it still works with a real re-sign, then deployed the cert to Proxmox's web UI (no more self-signed warning)

Two more isolated VLAN20 LXCs (droppdd-prod, unbrokerrdd), same pattern as web01 - droppdd's real production DB/secrets migrated off box, unbrokerrdd deployed fresh, both added to web01's existing tunnel as new ingress hostnames + DNS records
Cloudflare Access enabled in front of both new public apps (account was already Zero Trust-enrolled, zero setup cost) - verified end-to-end via browser, real email-OTP login gate confirmed on both

Home Assistant (192.168.20.183) given a real trusted cert via a second OPNsense ACME validation entry scoped to alwaysgivealwaysget.com (a fresh Cloudflare token - the original nunchimangchi.com token is zone-locked, always needed its own). Two automation actions (SFTP cert upload, SSH-triggered HA restart) needed separate SSH key algorithms - OPNsense reuses one keypair per algorithm across actions, so both on ed25519 caused the restart command to get shadowed by the SFTP action's forced-command authorized_keys line. Live cert independently verified via direct TLS connection, not just trusted from the report.

Added an internal-only AdGuard rewrite for ha.alwaysgivealwaysget.com -> 192.168.20.183, plus Tailscale Split DNS (nameserver 192.168.10.1, restricted to the alwaysgivealwaysget.com domain) so it resolves correctly on cellular too - both verified with live DNS queries, not just config review

Caught and fixed a real regression from the AdGuard step above: the rewrite was first added as a wildcard (*.alwaysgivealwaysget.com), which combined with the new Tailscale Split DNS to hijack droppdd/unbrokerrdd's subdomains to Home Assistant's IP for anyone on the home network or tailnet (public internet visitors were unaffected - they never touch AdGuard). Narrowed to an explicit ha.alwaysgivealwaysget.com entry only, matching the existing per-host convention already used for int.nunchimangchi.com. Found by explicitly re-checking droppdd/unbrokerrdd after the DNS change, not assumed safe.

HA's internal_url/external_url were stale (plain HTTP, wrong subnet IP from an earlier dual-homing setup) - updated both to https://ha.alwaysgivealwaysget.com:8123 (same value for both, since split-horizon DNS + Tailscale Split DNS collapses the home/away distinction to one hostname). Verified end-to-end via the real hostname: correct Let's Encrypt cert, HTTP 200 - the actual path the iOS Companion App takes, not just the raw IP.

phases.title: Onboarding UX audit (cold-visitor persona walkthrough)
phases.summary: Walked the actual live app end-to-end as a specific persona - "I got this link/invite from a Reddit post, clicked it, and..." - rather than reviewing in the abstract. Every finding below was confirmed by reading the real code/config, not assumed. Two related findings (the unstyled AccessDenied error page, and the missing privacy/ToS consent step + new onboarding fields for age/height/meal preference) are tracked in more detail as session memory rather than duplicated here. The audit itself is done; the fixes below are backlog, not yet built. First round of fixes shipped 2026-08-26: a real consent gate (/welcome, Privacy Policy + Beta Terms), new profile fields (age/height/meal preference with unit toggles), privacy-reassurance copy, a branded auth-error page, and the dashboard's fake OMAD timer replaced with an honest placeholder. Second round shipped 2026-08-26: /signin now pitches the app (workouts, AI meals, wagers, leaderboard) before asking for OAuth, and the dashboard's WOD/meal picks actually rotate daily now instead of showing the same fixed catalog row forever. Third round shipped 2026-08-26: Cloudflare Access opened for droppdd specifically (bypass decision, not just a widened allowlist - verified this removes the extra Access login prompt entirely rather than just accepting any identity through it), so real beta invites (friends, eventually Reddit) can reach droppdd's own sign-in directly. 8 of 9 original findings resolved - only pre-onboarding read-only browsing remains, still explicitly deferred by the maintainer. One new finding surfaced 2026-08-26 in conversation (not part of the original 9): droppdd's only auth provider is Google (confirmed via src/auth.ts), and /signin never mentioned that before the button - a user without a Google account would bounce silently with zero visibility into why. Fixed with a one-line note before the click; a second auth provider was deliberately not built, disproportionate effort for a beta this size.

steps.label: Cloudflare Access opened for droppdd: policy decision changed from allow-one-email to bypass (Access stops intercepting the request at all), scoped to droppdd only - unbrokerrdd keeps its Access gate since unbrokerrdd has no auth of its own and its admin/viewer roles literally depend on Access's authenticated-user header for identity. droppdd's own real gate (Google OAuth + AllowedEmail) is unaffected and independently verified still enforcing (307 on /admin). First attempt (widening the policy's include to "everyone" while keeping decision "allow") was tried and checked live first - still showed an extra Cloudflare login prompt (any email could complete it, but it was still there) - corrected to "bypass" once that gap was surfaced
No landing/marketing content anywhere - /signin IS the landing page, asks for a Google OAuth grant before explaining what droppdd even is
/choose-username never explains the username is publicly visible on the leaderboard and to wager opponents - real risk of picking a throwaway name they'd regret

/onboarding never reassures that raw weight stays private (only a relative % ever shows publicly) - real friction for a weight-loss app's most sensitive input, right after a signup flow with zero privacy framing
/onboarding is lbs-only, no kg option - excludes/annoys a chunk of a Reddit-scale audience - fixed: weight (lbs/kg) and height (in/cm) both get unit selectors now
Nothing in the app is viewable until username + onboarding are both complete - no low-commitment "look around first" path for a curious cold visitor

Dashboard's "FASTING WINDOW (OMAD)" card - the largest, most prominent element on the homepage - is 100% static mock data (mockOMAD in src/lib/mock-data.ts), presented as a live countdown, identical for every user forever
"STREAK 🔥 ACTIVE & STRONG" and "0.0 LBS SHED TOTAL" read oddly at the guaranteed day-one zero state every new user starts at
"Today's WOD" and "upcoming meal" are prisma.findFirst() with no filter - the same fixed catalog row for every user, every day, not actually daily or personalized despite the framing

Google is droppdd's only auth provider with zero fallback - a user without a Google account isn't hard-blocked (Google's own login lets you create an account against any email) but got no warning before the click and would bounce with zero visibility. Fixed: one line above the sign-in button sets the expectation up front

phases.title: Wagers UX audit (solo + peer-challenge persona walkthrough)
phases.summary: Continued the persona walkthrough into /wagers - the newest, most complex flow. Six real findings, all fixed same session, no schema changes needed. Biggest one: accepting a peer challenge was a single click with zero confirmation and used the wrong person's stats in the metric picker; both fixed with a new review/confirm page.

steps.label: Metric dropdown showed the challenger's own current stats even when challenging someone else, directly contradicting the helper text below it ('resolved against their progress, not yours') - fixed: dropdown is now generic, creator's stats shown once in a separate reference strip

Accepting a challenge was one click with zero confirmation - new /wagers/respond/[id] review page shows exactly what accepting means (computed against the challenged user's own live progress) before they can confirm

A guardrail-rejected accept (unsafe pace) dumped the user back to a generic /wagers error banner, leaving the challenge PENDING with no visible explanation - now stays in context on the review page with the specific warning and real next steps
Wager creation form wiped itself entirely on any validation error (typo'd username, aggressive pace) - submitted values now echo back through the redirect and prefill the form
Solo vs. peer-challenge mode read as one more optional field, not a real fork - now behind a visible '— OR CHALLENGE SOMEONE ELSE INSTEAD —' divider with its own submit button
Active/resolved wager cards showed bare unlabeled numbers (ambiguous for streak targets) - new formatMetricValue() helper renders '180 LBS' / '30 DAYS' consistently

phases.title: Daily check-in - the app's core progress loop was missing
phases.summary: Continued the persona walkthrough into an area the maintainer raised directly: how do users update their weight after onboarding? Answer, confirmed by grepping the whole codebase: they couldn't. currentStreak was set to 0 at signup and never incremented anywhere, ever - the dashboard/Navbar/leaderboard streak numbers were permanently frozen at 0 for every user, and WEIGHT_TARGET wagers could only ever resolve LOST, never WON, since currentWeight never moved past onboarding. This was the app's actual core premise not functioning past day one.

steps.label: Confirmed with the maintainer before building: streak = consecutive calendar days checked in (not tied to workouts or OMAD adherence)
WeightRecord.recordedAt (real DateTime) added alongside the existing cosmetic date string, which has no year and isn't reliable for date math - safe additive migration
New /checkin route + Navbar entry (placed right after Dashboard - now the most important recurring action in the app)
src/lib/streak.ts: UTC calendar-day comparison helpers, same-day re-check-in updates today's entry instead of double-counting or duplicating
currentWeight now actually updates on check-in - leaderboard %, dashboard trend, and wager resolution are all real for the first time
Dashboard check-in CTA added; /progress now sorts weight history by real timestamp instead of row insertion order
Exercise/workout-completion logging explicitly deferred as a future feature per the maintainer's own call - WorkoutTracker's client-side-only checkboxes untouched

phases.title: Meals UX audit (static catalog + AI planner persona walkthrough)
phases.summary: Continued the persona walkthrough into /meals. Four real findings, all fixed same session. Biggest one: mealPreference was collected at onboarding but deliberately left unwired to avoid overclaiming - now it actually constrains AI generation, and a real vegetarian option exists in the static catalog for the first time (checked the 3 existing rows directly - every one was meat-based, guaranteed mismatch for any vegetarian beta tester). Also closed a request-timeout gap found during a follow-up conversation about AI placement, risk, and cost.

steps.label: mealPreference (VEGETARIAN/CARNIVORE) now actually constrains the Gemini prompt - previously collected and ignored

Added a real vegetarian catalog meal (checked all 3 existing rows directly: ribeye, salmon, bacon-and-eggs - zero vegetarian options existed) via a new scoped, idempotent upsert script - deliberately not prisma/seed.ts, which was found to wipe Workout/Meal/WeightRecord/Progress before reseeding (fine for dev, would have destroyed real prod check-in history)
Fixed leaked ops-facing error copy - end users were being told to verify process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY on a server they have no access to

60s per-user cooldown on AI generation (new User.lastAiMealGeneratedAt) - guards real billed Gemini API cost on a key already flagged as shared with box's own CLI tooling, spent only on real attempts, not validation failures

Follow-up from the AI risk/cost discussion: the Gemini call had no request timeout at all (a hung API response left users on the loading spinner forever) - added a 25s timeout (confirmed against the SDK's actual types), and fixed one more missed instance of the same error-leak pattern (raw SDK error message was being echoed straight to the client)

phases.title: Workouts UX audit (catalog + tracker persona walkthrough)
phases.summary: Continued the persona walkthrough into /workouts. Lighter than the others - the dominant issue (zero persistence, nothing survives a refresh) was already found and explicitly deferred as a future feature during the check-in audit, not re-flagged here. One new, independent finding, fixed.

steps.label: "FINISH WORKOUT & CLAIM VICTORY" required zero completed sets - fired unconditionally on click, letting a user claim victory (full celebration screen, calorie claim) having done nothing. Now disabled until every set across every exercise is checked off, with a live "N sets left" hint
Checked the rest-timer's fragile string-matching (.includes("120s")/"90s", defaulting to 60s) against real seeded data - not a live bug today, left as-is

phases.title: Profile + leaderboard UX audit
phases.summary: Continued the persona walkthrough into /profile and /leaderboard. Two real findings, both fixed, no schema changes needed - the fields already existed from the earlier onboarding pass.

steps.label: age/height/mealPreference were captured once at onboarding with zero edit path afterward - real gap now that mealPreference actively steers AI meal generation. New /profile form to update all three

A 'maintain weight' goal (targetWeight === startWeight, never prevented by onboarding's schema) divided by zero, rendering "NaN% TOWARD GOAL" on /progress and /leaderboard - fixed with a guard, and extracted the formula into a single shared src/lib/progress-percent.ts, closing a real drift risk (leaderboard's own comment claimed to reuse the formula but was actually a hand-copied duplicate)

phases.title: Admin panel audit (persona/purpose-driven, not just mechanical)
phases.summary: Audited /admin against what it's actually for, not just walked for bugs: access control (allowlist), catalog curation (workouts/meals CRUD), and a deliberately read-only per-user troubleshooting view - that read-only design is good and was kept, not loosened. One confirmed regression fixed. One larger finding - the Privacy Policy shipped earlier tonight promises account deletion/data export with zero admin tooling to actually do it - is now built: a separate /admin/users/[id]/data-rights flow (export first, consequence preview, two-step server-verified confirmation), deliberately kept off the existing read-only troubleshooting page rather than loosening it.

steps.label: /admin/users/[id] showed every weigh-in as year 2001 - confirmed directly (new Date("Aug 25").toLocaleDateString() -> 8/25/2001 in Node), a regression from rendering the old cosmetic date string instead of the real recordedAt timestamp added during check-in. Query ordering was also alphabetical on the string, not chronological. Both fixed

No tooling exists anywhere in the admin panel to fulfill the Privacy Policy's own promised account-deletion/data-export workflow - today that means hand-writing raw Prisma/SQL against prod with no confirmation step or audit trail. Design for a safety-railed flow, not yet built

Built the data-rights flow: /admin/users/[id]/export (Route Handler, deliberately outside /api since proxy.ts's middleware excludes that prefix from auth), consequence preview (flags active peer challenges specifically), required export-acknowledgement checkbox + typed exact-username confirmation (re-verified server-side, not trusted from the client). Cascade-delete mechanics verified empirically against dev data before building on top of them, not assumed. console.log audit trail, not a new DB table, given current scale

Beta-cap enforcement: the X/10 slot counter was cosmetic only - addAllowedEmail had no cap check, so the form kept accepting new operators past 10 with just an orange banner. Now rejects non-admin invites once BETA_USER_LIMIT (moved to its own src/lib/beta-limit.ts - a "use server" file can only export async actions, a plain constant there broke the build) is reached; admins are excluded from the cap. Deliberately a code-level limit requiring a redeploy to raise, not a UI toggle

phases.title: /why page - the founder's note
phases.summary: Direct maintainer request: a bottom-left, About-style link stating why droppdd was built, what makes it effective, the confidence that comes from being a real user, and a way to contact the maintainer. Content deliberately reuses the already-approved beta-invite email voice rather than drafting something new.

steps.label: New public /why route, excluded from the auth gate same as /legal/* - reachable without signing in

Entry points: desktop sidebar bottom-left (next to TERMINATE SESSION, visible regardless of auth state) and a matching icon in the mobile header - deliberately not added to the already-dense mobile bottom tab bar (8-9 icons), same precedent as sign-out's earlier move out of that bar
Contact link is a plain mailto: to the existing admin address - no new feedback infrastructure built, wasn't the ask

Deployed to droppdd-prod, verified live: /why returns 200 unauthenticated, / still 307s, visually confirmed on the real public domain (no dev-mode-badge artifact seen locally, since that only exists in next dev, not the production build)

phases.title: Self-serve feedback board (bugs, feature requests, discovery)
phases.summary: Prompted by a realization mid-conversation while planning Reddit outreach: there was no real answer to "how do testers give feedback" beyond the /why mailto link. Built a kanban-style board (NEW/PLANNED/IN_PROGRESS/DONE columns) covering bugs, feature requests, and discovery notes in one place - any signed-in operator can submit a card; status moves and deletion are admin-only.

steps.label: New BoardItem model (type + status as plain strings with documented allowed values, matching Wager's existing pattern - sqlite has no native Prisma enums) - purely additive migration, read directly before applying to prod
New /board route, gated same as every other page - open submission for any signed-in operator, since the whole point was closing the feedback gap, not curating it
Status moves and deletion admin-only (reused checkAdmin()) - a tester can flag something, only the maintainer decides where it stands
Static 4-column kanban (no drag-and-drop) - a deliberate scope call, proportional for a 10-person beta rather than pulling in a DnD library
Added BOARD to the main nav - flagged honestly: mobile bottom tab bar is now at 9-10 icons, the densest it's been. Not addressed here; a mobile-nav audit is separate future work

Full click-through actually performed locally before shipping - created, moved, and deleted a real card, not just build/lint. Deployed to droppdd-prod with an explicit confirmation before the migration; verified live

phases.title: AI meal planning: permanent swap from Gemini to Claude
phases.summary: Real outage, not a hypothetical: droppdd-prod's GEMINI_API_KEY is shared with box's own gemini CLI tooling (tracked tech debt since the original AI-meal-planning phase) and ran out of quota, unusable until Saturday. Rather than wait it out, swapped providers entirely on a dedicated key - closes the shared-key tech debt in the same move instead of just riding out this one outage.

steps.label: @google/generative-ai -> @anthropic-ai/sdk, model -> claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 (matches gemini-1.5-flash's fast/cheap role). Confirmed the SDK's real request-options timeout shape from installed package types before relying on it

No native JSON-only response mode on Claude (unlike Gemini's responseMimeType) - kept the existing "raw JSON only" prompt instruction (Claude follows it reliably) and added a defensive markdown-fence strip before parsing. Existing Zod validation of AI output (already treating it as untrusted) unchanged

Privacy Policy's AI-meal-planning section and the schema comment both updated to name the real processor (Anthropic, not Google) - a stale privacy policy naming the wrong third party would be a real accuracy problem

Found and flagged, not fixed here: npm install surfaced a pre-existing high-severity deepmerge-ts CVE via @prisma/config -> prisma, confirmed unrelated to this change (prisma's own pinned version untouched in the lockfile diff), needs a breaking major-version bump - separate work

Real deploy friction, resolved by verifying rather than assuming: the maintainer reported adding ANTHROPIC_API_KEY to prod twice, but the file's own mtime proved neither edit had actually landed - traced to editing the wrong location, not a code problem. Third attempt confirmed via mtime before proceeding

Real functional round-trip test performed on the live production site (not just build/lint): both entry points - pantry-driven and macro-driven, including grocery-list generation - generated real recipes via Claude, passed the existing Zod schema, and rendered correctly

phases.title: Fix: AI-generated recipe rendered in a narrow strip
phases.summary: First real bug filed on the new feedback board, by the maintainer. Generated recipes rendered inside the same 1/3-width AI-panel column as the input form - cramped and hard to read. Fixed by lifting generation state up so the result renders full-width, directly above the static meal catalog, instead of squeezed into the sidebar.

steps.label: Split AiMealPlanner.tsx into MealsInteractive.tsx - a Server Component (page.tsx) can't hold the generatedMeal/isLoading/error state, so it now just fetches meals and passes them down as a prop while the client component owns the full interactive layout
Result, loading skeleton, and error panel all moved to a full-width zone above the static catalog grid - the AI panel's own column is now form-only
Old AiMealPlanner.tsx deleted (confirmed via grep it was only ever imported from meals/page.tsx first) rather than left dangling
No markup rewritten from scratch - every card/section is the same JSX relocated, a layout fix not a redesign
Deployed to droppdd-prod and verified with a real generation on the live site (not just build/lint) - confirmed the result now renders full-width directly below the page header, above the static list
Closed the loop: moved the bug card to DONE on the feedback board itself, proving the board->fix->close cycle works end to end

career-ops.summary: A real, actively-used job-search tracker (private data - real applications, scores, notes), not a demo despite the original directory name. Worked jointly with a second Claude session ("Current salary floor") running on the user's Mac, where this project actually lives - box has no filesystem access to it except via a bridged SSH connection set up specifically for this.

phases.title: Fixed a real data-exposure risk
phases.summary: This was a clone of a public third-party template (santifer/career-ops) still pointing at that repo as origin, with real personal data untracked in the working tree - one git push away from landing in someone else's public GitHub.

steps.label: Created a new private repo (nunchimangchi-dev/career-ops) the user actually owns
Repointed origin to the private repo, kept the original template as a fetch-only upstream remote (push disabled) rather than discarding template-update capability entirely
Real personal data committed and pushed to the private repo, verified independently via the GitHub API (not just trusting the report)

phases.title: Tracker data cleanup
phases.summary: 144 files removed under an explicit criterion (never clicked through to an actual application, regardless of date) - not a date cutoff, which would have discarded real signal like an old application that got a response.

steps.label: Real inventory built before any deletion - exact counts, status-column semantics, named edge cases (a live warm lead, 3 untracked orphan reports) surfaced for explicit decisions rather than folded into the bulk criterion
Both edge cases decided explicitly by the user (kept the live lead, removed the orphans)

Peer session declined to execute off a relayed "user decided X" and got the user's own direct confirmation first - correct call, same standard held throughout this project for consequential/hard-to-reverse actions

Learned the hard way that "this repo has git history" isn't the same claim as "these specific files are tracked" - reports/ and output/ turned out to be gitignored, so this cleanup had no git safety net despite an earlier (wrong) reassurance that it did

phases.title: Design pass on pipeline-dashboard.html
phases.summary: Moved off the same generic dark-obsidian/cyan-neon aether-core.css palette unbrokerrdd's first pass also had to move away from, onto a bespoke "Slate & Steel-Blue" identity grounded in a real cited reference (Linear's dark theme). Also removed the Chart.js CDN dependency (a live third-party network signal every time a private tool got opened) by vendoring it locally.

steps.label: Drafted from the real file content (relayed with personal data sanitized to placeholders - the other session's own good judgment, not requested)

Run via Gemini in genuine interactive mode over a tmux session bridged from box - not blind headless -p (tool-restricted) and not unattended --yolo (a real trust decision the auto-mode classifier correctly flagged); Claude watched and approved each tool action live instead
Verified directly after the fact: real scoped commit, complete 205KB Chart.js bundle, JS logic/data/personal-identifier locations all confirmed untouched via diff
Merged to main; push blocked by an expired gh token on that Mac (human re-auth needed, not something to force through non-interactively)

decisions.title: skyrise repo is public
decisions.why: Concrete, current infra/dotfiles work is the resume signal; secrets never live in git so public is safe.

decisions.title: Dashboard is Tailscale-only
decisions.why: Personal build log has no reason to be internet-facing; tailnet already includes box, phone, and the MacBook.

decisions.title: chezmoi over stow/plain script
decisions.why: Needs to reconcile real Linux/macOS differences (paths, package managers) across two hosts with one source of truth.

decisions.title: Git commit email is GitHub's noreply address
decisions.why: Standard privacy practice — keeps the real iCloud address out of public commit metadata.

decisions.title: droppdd starts as a Next.js web app
decisions.why: Fastest path to something usable on a phone browser today; mobile app shell can wrap it later if needed.

decisions.title: MagicDNS short hostname deferred
decisions.why: Would need a systemd-resolved/NetworkManager fix, and Tailscale's auto-cert only covers the full .ts.net name anyway, so a short name would break HTTPS. Not worth it yet — full URL works fine.

decisions.title: Reboot verification confirmed full auto-recovery
decisions.why: Rebooted box and checked the dashboard service, tailscale serve, and tmux-continuum boot-restore against docs/POST-REBOOT-CHECKLIST.md — all came back with zero manual steps, closing out the tmux phase.

decisions.title: fish config switched from CachyOS's bundled theme to Starship
decisions.why: The old config.fish sourced a CachyOS-only package for its prompt, which doesn't exist on macOS — broke the one-source-of-truth goal before the Mac was even involved. Starship is genuinely cross-platform and turned out to already be the Mac's real prompt (it overrides Oh My Zsh's theme in the old .zshrc), so switching preserved the look the user already liked instead of losing it.

decisions.title: MacBook Pro bootstrap completed with fish as the default shell
decisions.why: Full bootstrap run (packages, git/gh identity, chezmoi dotfiles, tmux+tpm, fisher) plus the account-level shell switch — all confirmed with the user directly at each consequential step (dotfiles diff review, killing a pre-existing unrelated tmux session, the sudo/chsh commands run by the user themselves, never by an agent).

decisions.title: Homelab web server exposed only via Cloudflare Tunnel, never port-forwarded
decisions.why: No inbound firewall holes on the OPNsense edge for a personal project — the tunnel connector makes an outbound-only connection, so there's nothing for a scanner to find regardless of what's running behind it.

decisions.title: New webserver LXC gets its own isolated VLAN, not the Proxmox/OPNsense management network
decisions.why: A publicly-reachable service (even behind a tunnel) shouldn't have L2 access to anything sensitive if it's ever compromised — real segmentation, not just faith in the tunnel.

decisions.title: SSH key-based auth set up for Proxmox before doing anything else
decisions.why: The root password was retrieved from Bitwarden and used directly in the user's own terminal — never pasted into chat, never touched by the agent. Matches the same credential-handling discipline as every other host in this project.

decisions.title: Added a narrow firewall exception (port 53 only) from VLAN20 to the AdGuard Home resolver on the mgmt network, instead of rebinding AdGuard to every VLAN
decisions.why: AdGuard Home was only ever bound to the mgmt interface (192.168.10.1) — VLAN20/30 clients had no working DNS at all. A scoped DNS-only carve-out in the existing isolation rule keeps the rest of the isolation intact rather than widening AdGuard's listen scope.

decisions.title: Reset alwaysgivealwaysget.com's zone security_level from under_attack back to medium
decisions.why: Leftover from the domain's earlier compromised state — it was silently JS-challenging every request, including the tunnel's own traffic, before the new legitimate site could ever be reached.

decisions.title: Internal DNS uses int.nunchimangchi.com (real subdomain), not a .lan TLD
decisions.why: A .lan/.local TLD can never get a publicly-trusted CA cert. A real subdomain that's only ever registered in internal DNS (never published in public DNS) gets valid, no-warning HTTPS internally the technically correct way — and it already matched OPNsense's own existing hostname convention (fw1.int.nunchimangchi.com).

decisions.title: Verified the existing ACME DNS-01 token instead of rotating it on sight
decisions.why: Found a live Cloudflare-scoped token already wired into OPNsense's ACME client, last used successfully 3 weeks prior — rather than assume it was the deleted/compromised one from the earlier account cleanup, did a real functional test (triggered an actual cert re-sign) to confirm it's a distinct, still-valid token before relying on it.

decisions.title: Closed the loop on cert renewal instead of a one-time manual push
decisions.why: The wildcard cert was renewing correctly but nothing restarted the services using it — OPNsense's own GUI was silently serving a stale cached cert. Wired the built-in "restart web UI" action, and configured a real least-privilege Proxmox API token (Sys.Modify on /nodes/pveopti only) so future renewals auto-push to Proxmox too. Also enabled real HTTPS on AdGuard Home's admin UI (was plain HTTP) and wired its restart into the same chain. Verified with a real re-sign — OPNsense, Proxmox, and AdGuard all picked up the identical new cert serial automatically, no manual steps.

decisions.title: droppdd and unbrokerrdd moved to real public hosting on memorable subdomains, not Tailscale
decisions.why: A Tailscale Funnel *.ts.net URL was considered first (fastest path to a public link) but rejected: it isn't memorable, and someone shown droppdd in person has no way to recall or revisit a ts.net address later. Real subdomains of the already-owned alwaysgivealwaysget.com (droppdd.*, unbrokerrdd.*) reuse the proven Cloudflare Tunnel infrastructure from web01, each app on its own isolated VLAN20 LXC per the same isolation principle — not a shortcut, the same pattern extended.

decisions.title: droppdd's production instance migrated off box onto its own isolated LXC (droppdd-prod)
decisions.why: Production had been running as a systemd --user service directly on box, reachable only via tailscale serve — box can't be reached by web01's tunnel without punching a hole through the VLAN20-to-management isolation that's the whole point of this design. Migrated the real database and secrets (not a fresh reseed) onto a new LXC on VLAN20, verified `prisma migrate deploy` reported zero pending migrations post-copy before cutting over.

decisions.title: Cloudflare Access gates both public apps, not just app-level login
decisions.why: unbrokerrdd's dashboard has no authentication of its own at all, so Access stays fully enforced there (allowlisted: owner only) and denies unauthenticated requests before they reach the origin. droppdd's own Google OAuth + allowlist gate turned out to be the real access-control layer once it existed - keeping Access double-gated on top of it started blocking real beta invites for no added security, so on 2026-08-26 droppdd's Access policy was changed to bypass (Access stops intercepting the request at all), scoped to droppdd only. See the onboarding-ux-audit phase for the full verification (droppdd's own auth confirmed still enforcing, unbrokerrdd confirmed untouched).

decisions.title: Per-app admin panel is a tracked requirement, not solved by Cloudflare's dashboard
decisions.why: Cloudflare Access's own dashboard is the only way to add/remove allowed users right now (see docs/RUNBOOK-ADD-USER-CLOUDFLARE-ACCESS.md) — functional, but explicitly called out as not good enough long-term: it's invisible from either app and doesn't demonstrate real full-stack (L1-L7) ownership of the access-control layer. Backlog: a real admin view in each app, with Access staying on as the outer gate regardless (defense in depth, not a replacement).

decisions.title: unbrokerrdd trusts Cloudflare Access's identity header instead of building its own login
decisions.why: Unlike droppdd (real multi-user data models, peer wagers coming), unbrokerrdd is single-tenant — one campaign, no per-user data to scope. A second login system (OAuth, password) would duplicate what Access already does at the edge. The app reads Cf-Access-Authenticated-User-Email directly and maps it to a viewer/admin role in its own allowed_users table — safe only because the app has no public port-forward and is unreachable except through the tunnel Access sits in front of.

decisions.title: Gemini's unbrokerrdd admin-panel backend was verified directly, then its missing frontend was built by hand rather than re-prompted blind
decisions.why: The backend pass was genuinely solid — real passing tests, correct last-admin invariant, correct concurrency guard — but shipped zero UI despite the prompt asking for admin views/forms, and HANDOFF.md never flagged the gap. Once a backend contract is stable and well-tested, wiring a UI to it is comparatively low-risk, fast-to-verify work — built directly and visually confirmed live rather than spending another blind Gemini round on it.

decisions.title: A second Claude session (network-ops-02) did the HA/OPNsense-ACME work; every specific claim it made was independently re-verified before being treated as done
decisions.why: Cross-session work isn't self-verifying just because it reads as detailed and confident — the same discipline applied to Gemini's HANDOFF.md claims applies here too. Checked the live cert directly (TLS connection, not trusting the report), then once given scoped OPNsense API access, checked every UUID/config detail named (validation entry zone-scoping, both automation actions, the dual-SSH-key-algorithm workaround) against the real config. Everything matched exactly — a good outcome, but only because it was actually checked, not assumed.

decisions.title: OPNsense/AdGuard credentials were handed over as an SSH public key add, not a password or private key over chat
decisions.why: Box already had an established SSH keypair used for every other host in this project - adding its public key to fw1's authorized_keys via the OPNsense web UI meant no secret ever had to be typed or pasted into the conversation at all, safer than the alternative of relaying a password through chat even though that channel was already being used for other credentials tonight.

decisions.title: AdGuard's alwaysgivealwaysget.com rewrite is a single explicit host entry (ha.alwaysgivealwaysget.com), not a wildcard
decisions.why: First attempt used a wildcard (*.alwaysgivealwaysget.com -> Home Assistant's IP) for convenience - broke droppdd/unbrokerrdd's subdomains for anyone resolving through AdGuard or Tailscale Split DNS (home network, tailnet), since the same domain already has real public subdomains that need to resolve to Cloudflare's tunnel, not to Home Assistant. Caught by explicitly re-testing droppdd/unbrokerrdd after the DNS change rather than assuming a DNS change to one host doesn't affect others under the same domain. Fixed by matching the explicit per-host pattern already used for int.nunchimangchi.com's rewrites.

decisions.title: TECH DEBT (tracked, not forgotten): droppdd-prod's GEMINI_API_KEY reuses box's own gemini CLI key rather than a dedicated one
decisions.why: Deliberate speed tradeoff, made explicitly - user chose to move fast rather than provision a second key, and asked to be reminded later. A shared key means droppdd's real end-user-facing usage and box's own agentic coding/design-pass usage can't be monitored or rate-limited independently - a runaway-cost bug on one side could affect the other, with no clean way to revoke just one. Not urgent (both work fine today), but should be split into two dedicated keys next time this project comes up.

decisions.title: Privacy scope correction: required usernames before leaderboard identity, plus peer wagers
decisions.why: Mid-build on the leaderboard (before any code was written), the maintainer flagged that display identity needed a real fix first: every user must have a required, unique, changeable username, and the leaderboard should key off that instead of name/email. Also requested tracking peer wager challenges (accepted/won/lost/rejected) on each user's profile - this turned out to be Phase 2 of the project's own existing docs/FUTURE-WAGERS.md roadmap (peer wagers, still no money), not yet built. Avatar selection was explicitly scoped as "eventually", not now. Sequencing chosen: username system -> peer wagers -> leaderboard resume, since the leaderboard's identity display depends on the first.

decisions.title: Peer-wagers Gemini prompt abandoned after 3 stalls; built directly instead
decisions.why: The drafted GEMINI-PEER-WAGERS-PROMPT.md prompt stalled at 30+ minutes with zero tool calls on three consecutive attempts - twice on Auto model routing (which silently picked gemini-3.1-pro-preview), once pinned explicitly to gemini-3.5-flash. Every prior Gemini run this session had produced a first tool call within seconds, so this was a genuine anomaly, not normal variance. Since the prompt itself already fully specified the schema, the lifecycle, the authorization check, and the accept-time-vs-creation-time guardrail decision, there was nothing left to gain from a fourth retry - implemented directly against that same spec instead, with the same discipline (build+lint passing, migration SQL read directly before trusting it, unauthenticated smoke test before merging).

decisions.title: Found and fixed: droppdd's progress-tracking never actually worked past onboarding
decisions.why: Continuing the persona walkthrough, the maintainer asked directly how users update their weight after signup. Checked the code rather than assume: WeightRecord.create was only ever called once, at onboarding. Further check: currentStreak is set to 0 at onboarding and grepping the entire src tree found zero places anything ever increments it - the streak shown everywhere (dashboard, Navbar, leaderboard) was permanently 0 for every user, and WorkoutTracker's set-completion checkboxes are pure client-side state with no persistence at all. This meant WEIGHT_TARGET wagers could only ever resolve LOST (via time expiry), never WON, since the number they're measured against never moved. Built a real daily check-in flow (streak defined as consecutive check-in days, confirmed with the maintainer first since it wasn't specified) that fixes both weight and streak tracking at once. Exercise-completion logging deliberately left as a tracked future feature per the maintainer's explicit call, not bundled into this fix.

decisions.title: Real-money wager phases dropped from the roadmap, not deferred
decisions.why: Came up during an App Store feasibility discussion - real money would drag droppdd into Apple's strict, inconsistent gambling-review stance on peer-vs-peer stakes if it ever went native. But the deciding factor was independent of App Store concerns: the maintainer's own lived experience is that people motivated enough to game a real-money fitness stake will just settle up outside the app anyway - a workaround he ran himself for years against Fitbit's own step-based incentives. The legal/compliance cost of building real custody-adjacent payment flows buys less real enforcement than it looks like on paper. docs/FUTURE-WAGERS.md updated to mark phases 3-4 dropped; the free honor-system peer wager (phases 1-2, both already shipped) is now the permanent shape of this feature. Also surfaced two longer-horizon product wishes in the same conversation: push notifications (streak reminders, wager-opponent check-ins) as the near-term next step, and Apple Health/Fitness integration further out - both future work, not scheduled.
